note: 012 v2 (remake 2026-11-28 after Bidhan: 'felt like it went on forever', 'comparisons not relatable', 'not funny', 'ends abruptly, add Follow for...'). Weather show, Sarah (presenter) + Joseph (fed-up reporter, gets the punchlines). No size comparisons; Nile + flies + dry lake kept as jokes; spoken follow line at the end.
lines: This lake makes its own thunderstorm. Every. Single. Night.
This lake makes its OWN THUNDERSTORM. Every. Single. NIGHT.
[sighs] I know. I'm standing in it.
I know. I'm STANDING in it.
Welcome to How On Earth Weather! Joseph, how's Lake Victoria tonight?
Welcome to HOW ON EARTH WEATHER! Joseph, how's LAKE VICTORIA tonight?
Wet. The Nile starts at this lake... and apparently, so does every storm.
WET. The NILE starts at this lake... and apparently, so does EVERY STORM.
Here's the trick. By day, the sun cooks the land, so the storms happen over there.
Here's the TRICK. By DAY, the SUN cooks the LAND, so the STORMS happen over THERE.
[laughs] So daytime is a lovely beach day!
So DAYTIME is a lovely BEACH DAY!
Then at night, the land cools down... but the lake stays warm.
Then at NIGHT, the LAND cools down... but the LAKE stays WARM.
So breezes from every shore rush to the middle... and crash.
So BREEZES from EVERY SHORE rush to the MIDDLE... and CRASH.
[surprised] Every shore? At once? That's a whole gang!
EVERY SHORE? At ONCE? That's a whole GANG!
The warm, wet air shoots up... and builds a thunderstorm. Right on top of you.
The WARM, WET air shoots UP... and builds a THUNDERSTORM. Right on TOP of you.
[sarcastic] Fantastic. Any good news in the forecast?
FANTASTIC. Any GOOD NEWS in the FORECAST?
Flies! Lake flies. Billions of them, in clouds you can see from miles away.
FLIES! LAKE FLIES. BILLIONS of them, in CLOUDS you can see from MILES away.
[sarcastic] Cloudy... with a chance of flies. Love that for me.
CLOUDY... with a CHANCE of FLIES. Love that for ME.
Fun fact: seventeen thousand years ago, this whole lake was completely dry.
FUN FACT: 17 THOUSAND YEARS ago, this whole lake was COMPLETELY DRY.
[mischievously] Dry? Can it do that again... tonight, please?
DRY? Can it do that AGAIN... TONIGHT, please?
Sorry, Joseph. The storm's booked. Every single night.
SORRY, Joseph. The STORM'S BOOKED. Every single NIGHT.
[sighs] Then follow for more... I'll be under this umbrella.
Then FOLLOW for MORE... I'll be under this UMBRELLA.
